subject: Costing sprint & token ask — NovoHealth pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@novohealth.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@novohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-30T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Costing sprint & token ask — NovoHealth pilot

Hi Asha / Carlos — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we’re aligned heading into the costing sprint: 

Summary of asks / constraints from the call:
- Volume profile: baseline ~120M tokens/month, expected burst up to ~45M/day during training/ingestion windows.
- Target latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms for chat flows, offline batch embeddings can be higher.
- Data residency: primary region US, but requirement to support EU-siloed data for PHI-looking tenants.
- Budget signal: you mentioned target unit economics for pilot procurement in the ballpark of a single-digit thousands monthly commit, with a desired unit price of roughly $/1M tokens in the mid-hundreds (you said ~"a few hundred per 1M tokens"). We need to solidify a target range to model ROI.

Preliminary benchmarking request I captured (so we can model tradeoffs):
- Please confirm target $/1M tokens anchor you'd be comfortable with (range preferred).
- Confirm expected read/write proportion and typical sequence lengths (chat avg 450 tokens, system prompts + context ~600 tokens).
- Any hard constraints on model family (open LLM vs Anthropic-like vs Anthropic/Claude or OpenAI?suffices)?

What Redwood will produce in the costing sprint (deliverables):
1) A 3-tier cost model with per-1M token anchors (hosted, dedicated-reserved, private/VPC) with assumptions called out.
2) Sensitivity runs showing how KV-prefix caching and quantization change $/1M token estimates for your workload shape.
3) A short operations note: expected latency, recommended rollout (canary + fallback), and region routing options for EU compliance.

Attachments: attached our MVP scope doc and an initial token modeling workbook. Ben will follow up with a quick model that shows target-$/1M scenarios vs OpenAI and Anthropic public list pricing — we’ll annotate where caching/quantization change the math.

Next steps:
- Ben to drop the initial workbook by EOD (attached).
- Laura to coordinate a 45-min procurement + security sync w/ your team (proposed Wed 10/6).
- You to confirm the target $/1M anchor range; we’ll run the costing sprint to align on a recommended procurement tier.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Costing sprint & token ask — NovoHealth pilot

Adding the modeling perspective here — Jordan, Laura: attaching the workbook I mentioned. Highlights from a quick pass against the 120M tokens/mo profile: 

- Public host comps (ballpark, list/publicized):
  * OpenAI (gpt-4 style + embeddings mix): ~ $800–$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on mix of chat vs completion and streaming overhead.
  * Anthropic-like managed: ~ $600–$900 per 1M tokens at list (varies by model complexity).
  * Open-model hosts (quantized, high-density infra): ~ $250–$420 per 1M tokens for high-throughput workloads (these rely on aggressive quantization + batch optimizations).

- Redwood delta: for your workload shape (avg seq ~500–600, high prefix reuse from prompts) we expect:
  * Hosted: ~$520–$700 per 1M tokens (includes managed infra and fallbacks)
  * Dedicated reserved pool (12–24 month commit): ~$320–$420 per 1M tokens using int8/4 quantization + prefix KV caching
  * Private/VPC (on-prem partner): variable; ballpark similar to dedicated once infra amortized ($300–$450/1M).

Key levers that move the needle:
- KV/prefix caching: can cut served token compute by ~25–40% when prompts reuse system/context across sessions.
- Quantization profile: model-specific; int8 for many decoder-only models gives ~1.6–2x cost improvement vs fp16.
- Batching and sequence packing: workload-dependent but can further reduce per-token cost for high throughput bursts.

Quick asks for a cleaner run: can Asha confirm the percent of messages with shared system prompt/contexts (we think 40–60% reuse), and whether embeddings are batched/offline vs on-demand (impacts GPU amortization)?

Attaching workbook: redwood_token_modeling.xlsx — I filled a scenario with a $/1M target sweep from $250 to $1,000 and a column that shows which Redwood deployment mode would economically make sense for each anchor.

If you want, I can produce a short 1-page benchmark slide that lines up OpenAI / Anthropic / Open-hosts and shows the Redwood recommendation with the sensitivity bands.

Ben
Senior Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment stub: redwood_token_modeling.xlsx (see workbook tab "NovoHealth_scenarios")

From: Asha Rao <asha@novohealth.com>

Subject: Re: Costing sprint & token ask — NovoHealth pilot

Thanks Jordan & Ben — this is excellent, and the workbook looks useful. A few clarifications from our side so you can zero the model in: 

1) Target $/1M anchor: For the pilot procurement (3 months), our procurement team will greenlight anything under $450/1M as a baseline; ideal is $300–$400/1M — if you can show how Redwood hits those numbers in a realistic configuration we’ll have a good path to sign.

2) Workload notes:
  - Shared prompt reuse: ~55% of sessions reuse the same system prompt + persona, so KV/prefix caching looks promising.
  - Embeddings: primarily offline batch for customer ranking (nightly), but on-demand embeddings for a small percentage (<10%) of sessions.
  - Sequence length: median ~420 tokens, 95th ~1,800 tokens.

3) Compliance / SLO asks for pricing scenarios: please call out the price delta for EU-siloed processing and for an SLA with a 99.9% uptime commitment.

4) Can you add a column that shows an amortized per-1M cost with a $50k/month reserved commit vs a $10k/month reserved commit? That will help procurement with internal thresholds.

Also please include a quick note on what would be required for a stop-loss clause (e.g., overspend protection / daily rate caps) — procurement is sensitive to runaway inference costs.

If you can get a tightened 3-tier (hosted / dedicated 10–50k commit / private) by EOD Friday we can slot a procurement + security call next Wed.

Best,
Asha
VP Product | NovoHealth
asha@novohealth.com
